reasoning_content:
Interesting — `ss -ltn` didn't show anything (not even any LISTEN lines?). Actually, the first `ss -ltn | grep -E "8080|LISTEN"` didn't output anything, and "=== all listens ===" didn't show any ss output either. So either `ss` is not installed, or there's no listener. Let me check whether `ss` is available and try directly with /proc/net/tcp.

No wait — the `ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E "8080|LISTEN"` command output nothing (stderr is suppressed). The "=== all listens ===" section also showed nothing. Which means `ss` may not exist (output suppressed). Let me check /proc/net/tcp for port 8080 (0x1F90), and try curl once more with a short timeout.

action.command: cd /workspace && command -v ss; echo "---/proc/net/tcp (8080=1F90)---" && grep -i ":1F90" /proc/net/tcp /proc/net/tcp6 2>/dev/null; echo "exit:$?"; echo "---curl---"; curl -s -m 8 -o /dev/null -w "info:%{http_code} time:%{time_total}\n" http://localhost:8080/api/v1/info; echo "curl exit:$?"; echo "---process tree---"; ps -ef | grep -E "21562|21596|badge" | grep -v grep
